title: Plausibility under Rule 8
summary: Plausibility asks whether the well-pleaded factual allegations support a reasonable inference of entitlement to relief in the context of the claim. Legal labels and recitations of elements do not supply missing facts.
notes: This is not trial proof or a requirement that the plaintiff establish a probability of winning. Nor does it authorize the judge to treat well-pleaded facts as false because the judge prefers another account. The separate opinions and Swanson show substantial disagreement in application.

sections.Meaning: Plausibility asks whether the well-pleaded factual allegations support a reasonable inference of entitlement to relief in the context of the claim. Legal labels and recitations of elements do not supply missing facts.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the claim’s required elements, separate conclusory statements from factual allegations, accept well-pleaded facts, and assess what those facts plausibly support. Explain why a factual detail bears on the needed inference.
